As required by R5, the ratio is used as reported and not recomputed. The value is well away from both boundaries, so the table gap at exactly L/D = 3 does not matter.

d2.justification: The external diameter sequence from axial 0 is 29.9 / 60 / 100 / 50 mm. The maximum diameter is interior, with 2 diameter changes toward axial 0 and 1 toward axial max, so the outer contour steps down toward both ends. An external thread exists on the long Ø50 section: the CAD model shows helical faces near Ø50 spanning about 82.7 to 210 mm, and the human-verified drawing callout confirms a thread with pitch 5 over a threaded length of 125 on the Ø50 shaft. Grooves are absent in the evaluated geometry. Chamfers and conical faces are also absent, so there is no functional cone. Thread is therefore the most specific supported shape element on a part stepped at both ends.

d3.justification: There is a continuous axial opening from end to end, so the part has a through bore and row 0 is excluded. The evaluated internal coaxial diameters from axial 0 are Ø12 (0-41.42), Ø13 (41.42-170) and Ø30 (170-210) mm. This sequence never decreases, so every step faces the axial-210 end, which reads as stepped on one end. An internal thread is reported in the CAD model: a threadCreator feature with pitch 2 mm and helical faces near Ø12/Ø13 spanning about 0-42.3 mm at the axial-0 end. On the evaluated diameters, the most specific supported element is therefore stepped on one end with thread.

threadCreator thread, pitch 2 mm, full length; helical faces near diameters 12/13 mm over about 0-42.3 mm; status known, confidence medium

d3.uncertainty_reason: (a) The internal thread is evidenced only in the CAD model. No human-verified drawing fact confirms it on the physical part, unlike the external thread. (b) The thread's major (root) diameter is not measured: the helical faces are located only by loose bounding boxes, and the threadCreator majorDiameter of 25 mm is inconsistent with the geometry. The Hole feature parameter is 14 mm, while the evaluated cylinder is Ø12. If the thread root exceeds the Ø13 mid-bore, the bore would be larger at both ends than in the middle, which would mean stepped both ends (row 5). Not used as evidence (R4), but worth checking: the reported thread label '0.5118-12.7' converts to 13 mm / 2 mm pitch, which would keep row 2. (c) A Ø12 entrance followed by a larger Ø13 bore is unusual and should be confirmed on the section view.

competing_candidates.why_not_chosen: Stepped both ends with thread. This holds only if the internal thread's major diameter is larger than 13 mm; the evaluated diameters (12, 13, 30) are monotonic and the thread major diameter is not measured, per R9.

Stepped both ends, no shape elements. This would need both no internal thread on the drawing and a both-ends stepping interpretation; neither is supported.

d4.justification:
Three planar faces parallel to the rotation axis lie on the Ø29.9 end section (axial 0-20):
- one face 17.9 mm from the axis, area 159.6 mm², which is 7.98 mm × 20 mm;
- two faces at ±3.99 mm, each about 3.49 mm high.
The outer face lies outside the Ø29.9 cylinder (radius 14.95 mm), so together the three faces bound a single rectangular raised projection, about 7.98 mm wide, on the small end. These are external plane surfaces. They are not grooves or slots, and they are not arranged by circular graduation, since two are parallel opposite faces and one is perpendicular to them. A single projection does not amount to a spline or polygon. No internal plane surfaces are reported.

overall_notes:
Proposed form code 15212. Reviewer focus, in order of risk:
(1) d3 has high uncertainty. Check on the section view whether the internal thread at the Ø12 end appears on the drawing, and whether its major diameter exceeds the Ø13 mid-bore; if so, d3 would become 5. If the thread is not on the drawing, d3 would become 1. The hole parameter (14 mm) disagrees with the evaluated Ø12, and both threadCreator features report majorDiameter 25 mm, which matches neither threaded region.
(2) d4 depends on how the course treats a single integral raised key-like projection (7.98 mm wide, outer face 17.9 mm from the axis, on the Ø29.9 section); row 1 is proposed, and rows 5 and 9 are alternatives.
(3) Feature inventory index 7 ('Extrude 1', FnFiH5Y4UDMPGEo_1) is not attributed to any fact in the manifest. Confirm it creates no feature relevant to d2-d5.
(4) d5 cites six hole faces, but the manifest's evidence list references only three face IDs (12, 14, 16), while count_of_cylinder_faces is 6. Count the holes on the drawing.
d1 and d2 are well supported. The d2 thread rests on human_supplied_facts[0], because facts.external_thread_on_physical_part is unknown and was not used. Labels and feature names were not used as evidence; the internal thread label is mentioned only as something to check. This is a proposal for human verification against the drawing and the manual worksheet.
